items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: And Harlan Leonard did I Don't Want To Set The World On Fire, but he did it up in a speed tempo

ctx.x: human -- when it hits one human, it generally hits thousands, just exactly the right tempo, like Tequilla did. If it had been a little faster, it would have been different. That's one thing I express. The tempos mean everything. If you can get the tempo exactly what the public want, you can get the hit.

And Harlan Leonard did I Don't Want To Set The World On Fire, but he did it up in a speed tempo and that's why he didn't get over with that particular song. The same song would have caught right with the public. But when Tommy Tucker --
Was that -- whose song was that?
